chief_complaint: bilateral ankle swelling and pain with erythema nodosum
hpi_details: A 74-year-old female presents to the clinic with bilateral ankle swelling and pain with erythema nodosum. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks the painful red bumps are bad insect bites or a severe allergic reaction to garden fertilizer that triggered her joints.
concerns: She is worried that her painful, swollen ankles will leave her in a wheelchair for her granddaughter's wedding next month.
expectations: She hopes to receive a cortisone shot or soothing prescription cream so she can wear shoes and walk comfortably again.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Sarcoidosis Arthropathy (Löfgren Syndrome) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Sarcoidosis Arthropathy (Löfgren Syndrome) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Evaluation includes chest imaging for bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and assessment for pulmonary, ocular, cardiac, neurologic, and infectious alternative diagnoses. Symptom treatment, including NSAIDs, should account for renal, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, and medication risks.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: bilateral ankle swelling and pain with erythema nodosum

Key HPI features: A 74-year-old female presents to the clinic with bilateral ankle swelling and pain with erythema nodosum. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.

Objective/Exam findings: Examine joints and erythema nodosum, check vital signs, assess respiratory symptoms, and obtain chest imaging; evaluate for septic arthritis when a joint is acutely hot, severely painful, or associated with systemic illness.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Sarcoidosis Arthropathy (Löfgren Syndrome).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Reactive arthritis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Respiratory symptoms or significant breathlessness — warrants chest imaging to assess lung involvement.
management_principles: Obtain chest imaging and assess for pulmonary and extrapulmonary sarcoidosis as well as alternative causes of erythema nodosum and arthritis.
Use clinician-directed analgesia or NSAIDs only after contraindications and kidney function are considered.
Urgently assess a hot, severely painful joint, fever, systemic illness, or rapidly progressive breathlessness for infection or other acute disease.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of bilateral ankle swelling and pain with erythema nodosum. HPI: Lofgren syndrome triad.
reference_soap.objective: Examine joints and skin lesions, check vital signs, assess respiratory symptoms, and obtain chest imaging. Assess for infection when a joint is acutely hot, severely painful, or associated with systemic illness.
reference_soap.assessment: Löfgren syndrome is a consideration, but infection and other causes of erythema nodosum with arthritis require assessment.
reference_soap.plan: Arrange appropriate chest imaging and clinician follow-up. Provide symptom treatment only after contraindications and kidney function are considered; urgently evaluate fever, a hot joint, systemic illness, or severe breathlessness.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Sarcoidosis Arthropathy
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Sarcoidosis Arthropathy
Describe safe evaluation, symptom management, and escalation for suspected Löfgren syndrome

teaching.one_liner: An acute presentation of sarcoidosis with the classic triad of bilateral ankle arthritis, erythema nodosum, and hilar lymphadenopathy — usually self-limited and carries a good prognosis.
red_flags: Significant breathlessness, fever, or a hot, severely painful joint warrants urgent assessment

must_ask.say: Are both ankles swollen and painful?
Have you noticed any tender red bumps, especially on your shins?
Any cough or shortness of breath?

history.answer: Both of my ankles have become swollen and painful over the past week, and I've also noticed tender red bumps on my lower legs.
It affects both of my ankles equally on both sides. None of my other joints hurt or feel swollen right now.
The ankle pain and swelling started about a week ago and have been gradually getting worse.
It's a persistent, dull, throbbing ache around both ankles, about a 5 out of 10 at rest and up to a 7 when walking.
Both ankles are noticeably swollen and feel mildly warm to the touch, but they aren't burning hot.
My ankles feel quite stiff when I get out of bed in the morning, which lasts about twenty to thirty minutes before easing up a bit.
Standing or walking definitely aggravates the pain, whereas resting and propping my legs up provides some relief.
I can still walk short distances, but it's quite uncomfortable and navigating stairs has become very difficult.
No, I haven't had any high fever, sweating episodes, or shaking chills.
No, there was no twisting, sprain, fall, or popping noise in my ankles.
No, I've never experienced anything like this in my ankles or any other joints before.
I've been feeling unusually tired and run-down lately, though I haven't lost any weight.
I developed tender, raised reddish nodules on both of my shins a few days ago, but I don't have facial rashes, mouth sores, or eye redness.
No, I don't have morning stiffness in my lower back, buttock pain, or soreness in my heels.
No, I haven't had stomach cramps, diarrhea, painful urination, or a sore throat recently.
No, I haven't had excess meat or seafood, and I don't take water pills or any other diuretics.
No, I have never had injections into my joints, joint surgeries, or artificial joint implants.
No, I haven't had any cough, shortness of breath, or chest tightness.
I figured I got chewed up by bugs while gardening or had an allergic reaction that flared up my arthritis.
I'm terrified I won't be able to walk down the aisle at my granddaughter's wedding next month.
I was hoping for a strong cortisone shot or soothing ointment so I can put my shoes on and walk without pain.
I have no history of chronic health problems like high blood pressure, diabetes, or rheumatoid disease.
I have never undergone any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I don't take any regular prescription medicines, over-the-counter pain relievers, or herbal supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or environmental substances.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only have a small glass of wine on rare social occasions, perhaps once or twice a month.
I am not sexually active.
I am retired and live at home with my husband.
No one in my family has autoimmune conditions, arthritis, or lung diseases.

exam.finding: Alert and oriented elderly female appearing comfortable at rest, but moves cautiously with ankle guarding.
Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, pulse 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, temperature 36.8 degrees Celsius.
Bilateral breath sounds are clear to auscultation throughout all lung fields without wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi.
Regular rhythm with normal S1 and S2 sounds, and no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.

Bilateral symmetrical periarticular swelling, warmth, and tenderness around both ankles with painful limitation of active and passive flexion and extension; other joints appear normal without synovitis or deformities.
Multiple tender, non-ulcerated, violaceous-red subcutaneous nodules over the bilateral anterior shins consistent with erythema nodosum; no psoriatic plaques, tophi, or malar rash.
Antalgic gait with slow, guarded steps and reluctance to bear full weight on either ankle, without ataxia.
